🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 4)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: code (NRE)  •  alerts in group: 3

*Symptoms:*
  • Centreon posted 3 CRITICAL service-checks to #alert-system (12:49:31–12:52:11Z).
  • method-platform-ui apps backend throwing `System.NullReferenceException` in `MethodSessionService.GetAccountBySubdomain()`, logged as *"JWT Retrieval Failed"* — 84 hits 12:50–13:10Z vs **0** same-window 24h-ago; sharp onset ~12:51Z.
  • *100% synthetic:* all 84 are WindowsPowerShell UA from 2 IPs (172.31.105.207 internal, 52.9.26.127 external), account id `0`, paths `/apps/api/{system/getsessiondata, dashboard/getdashboardrightpanel/0, outlookgadget/getnavigation/0, search/recents}`. **0 real-user (non-PowerShell) hits.**

Trace ID: dd_trace_id `6a198f4200000000d5495d4e2ab50634`
*Likely cause:* latent missing null-guard in `GetAccountBySubdomain()` (NREs when there is no resolvable subdomain). A synthetic monitor probe started hitting these endpoints subdomain-less at ~12:51Z and now reliably 500s them. No deploy (method-platform-ui last commit 23d); ms-authentication-api + gateway healthy. ⇒ **no real-user impact** — real users always carry a valid subdomain.
*Suggested next action:* file defect — either (a) null-guard `GetAccountBySubdomain()` to return 400/empty-session for a missing subdomain (source is TFS-built `Com.Method.ServiceContract`, not in the GitHub clones → route to platform-ui/MethodUI backend owner), or (b) fix the Centreon check to send a valid account subdomain/Host. Also confirm *why the probe changed at ~12:51Z* (Centreon check-config history).

Cross-bot corroboration: Datadog Watchdog `236570583` "New issue to review" fired 12:58:33Z for the same spike (group `25022f8c`).
📝 Added `kb/known-issues.json` → `ki-2026-05-29-methodsession-getaccountbysubdomain-nre` (fix_status: needs-human) so future Centreon/Watchdog fires dedup.

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-28-mobile-asyncstorage-securestore-keychain`
This is occurrence #3 (last DM'd >24h ago — suppression window elapsed, so resurfacing).

⚠️ *Sharp resurgence.* `"Failed to migrate from AsyncStorage to SecureStore" (ERR_KEY_CHAIN)` = *1612* errors in 15:01–15:35Z vs *58* in the same window 24h-ago = *27.8× spike*. Onset was sharp: 0 (15:00–15:20Z) → 1130 (15:20–15:31Z) → 482 (15:31–15:41Z). That burst is what fired Datadog Watchdog monitor `236570583` ("New issue to review", APM/infra) at 15:31:33Z in #alert-system.
*Attribution note:* this Watchdog fire is the mobile-keychain spike, **not** the NRE/ki-29 — `"JWT Retrieval Failed"` = 0 in window. Monitor 236570583 is generic, so it's attributed by dominant-anomaly + timing, not by reading the block.

*What it is:* Method iOS app (v2.1.537) one-time AsyncStorage→SecureStore keychain migration failing with iOS `ERR_KEY_CHAIN`. Client-side bug — *server has no fix*; route to the mobile team. No deploy correlation (method-nativemobile-ui HEAD 2026-04-30, 29d). No real customer-facing server fault.

Playbook: 1) Confirm volume + app version in ES (`fields.dd_service:"nonprod/apps"` + the message, check `fields.UserAgent` for `Method/2.1.537` + `CFNetwork/Darwin`=iOS). 2) CLIENT bug → mobile team; likely a missing/incorrect iOS keychain access-group/entitlement or a SecureStore key collision in the 2.1.537 migration path. 3) Mitigation: wrap the migration in try/catch and fall back to AsyncStorage (don't block app start on keychain), or fix the entitlement. 4) Server side: monitor volume only; consider down-ranking `/apps/v1/logging/mobile` to WARN to cut error-tracking noise.
Open Jira: none (fix_status: needs-human)

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-21-gateway-microservices-timeout`
This is occurrence #80 in the last 7 days — *every-10th-occurrence resurface* (so this long-running issue doesn't go invisible; last actual DM ~20h ago, otherwise still inside the 24h suppression window).

*Status: chronic, steady-state — NOT a new incident.* ES `Ocelot / RequestTimedOut / GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync` = *669* in window (15:15–16:08Z) vs *726* same-window 24h-ago = *−7.8%* (well under the 20% regression threshold). DNS (ki-dns) signature clean (0 hits). No deploy (ms-gateway-api 24d, runtime-core 23d). Monitor `77419271` (XHR errors) fired across 15:15–15:41Z; frontend XHR errors are the *symptom*, the cause is upstream ms-gateway-api Ocelot timeouts proxying to microservices.methodlocal.int (sync-util / preferences / account paths).

*fix_status: needs-ops-decision (unchanged)* — still your standing call:
 (a) raise per-route Ocelot timeout (cheapest, masks symptom), (b) scale / shorten recycle on the microservices IIS pool (addresses cold-start tail), or (c) profile the upstream microservice under prod load (root-cause, expensive).

Playbook: 1) Confirm chronic baseline (ES Ocelot Warning volume vs 24h-ago; delta <20% = chronic). 2) Aggregate timeouts by RequestPath — if dominant paths are all under microservices.methodlocal.int, it's pool-level. 3) Check ki-dns-microservices-method-int-pps-quota first (DNS bursts present here as Ocelot timeouts). 4) If DNS clean, identify the slow downstream via ocelot.*.json. 5) Fix decision tree (a/b/c above).
Open Jira: none

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring`
This is occurrence #30 in the last 7 days (resurfacing — last notified ~26.8h ago, past the 24h window).

*runtime-core-api RTC Screen Load / Action Execution p95 latency spike — latency-only, no errors.*
Fired #alert-runtime-monitoring 18:18:00 UTC (2 block-only Datadog msgs). This fire is *mild*: Screen Load p95 peaked 4.23s, Action Execution 4.57s (threshold 3s) — well below the 6.84s peak earlier today and the 24.4s peak on 05-24. Brief, self-resolving.

Playbook: 1) Confirm pattern via DD metric p95 on `post_/api/v1/runtime/load/_screenid*` + `/_actionid_*` — done: 4 / 2 points >3s in window. 2) Confirm latency-only via `service:runtime-core-api status:error env:prod` — done: 0 errors (DD + ES). 3) Diagnostic gap remains: identify the slow span via DD APM trace search (service:runtime-core-api @duration:>5s) in the spike window — look for SQL / Mongo aggregation / Redis SCAN dominating, break down by @account_name. 4) Mitigation options pending root cause: (a) raise monitor threshold to 4s if spikes stay short+sub-4s (cheapest, masks); (b) per-resource_name circuit breaker (medium); (c) profile slowest accounts + targeted SQL/Mongo index fixes (root cause, expensive).
Open Jira: none (fix_status: investigating)

Standing question for you: this signature has now fired 30× since 2026-05-23 with no errors and no deploy — it's monitoring-noise-adjacent. Worth either bumping the p95 threshold to 4s or committing to the APM-trace root-cause dig.
